files.purpose: Defines AppSettings, the @MainActor @Observable per-Mac preferences object that owns every app-wide user preference and writes each one to UserDefaults (WebsiteCaptures.defaults ?? .standard) from a didSet observer, reading them all back with explicit defaults in init(). It also defines the small enums and structs the Settings pages bind to (TextGenerationChoice, ThreadFinishAction, SidebarMode, ActivityThreadStyle, ModelPin, ModelPreference) with their visible titles and detail strings. Beyond flat preferences it owns the composer model list (max 15 pins, reorderable), per-model effort/fast-mode preferences, per-provider binary paths, disabled providers, last model/effort per provider, Hydra lead-and-heads pairs, per-project activation overrides, and the four API-key inputs (DeepSeek, Meta, Z.ai, Command Code) which live in the Keychain with a plaintext UserDefaults fallback and are read lazily or in the background. It conforms to ProviderSettings so the provider registry reads it.

The API-key didSets are the exception (next entries): they write the Keychain, and touch defaults only through storeAPIKeyFallback. Property observers do not run in init, so init never writes any value back (for example a normalized appZoom).

Setting an API key input (outside the fill) calls <Provider>Keychain.setAPIKey(value) with the UNTRIMMED input (e.g. `DeepSeekKeychain.setAPIKey(deepseekAPIKeyInput)`, line 370); if that returns true the defaults fallback key is removed (stored as ""), otherwise storeAPIKeyFallback writes `value.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)` to defaults in plaintext (lines 487-493). Trim asymmetry: the Keychain may hold leading/trailing whitespace, the fallback never does; apiKey(for:) trims on read (lines 907-910), but apiKeyInput(for:) returns the untrimmed value.

files.purpose: Implements the in-app self-update installer and the observable progress model the About page's version pill renders as a slider. UpdateInstallProgress is a forward-only progress state machine with milestone dots at 0.55, 0.70, 0.86 and 0.96, creep animation for phases without byte progress, haptics at milestones and a post-relaunch celebration sweep. AppUpdater downloads the release .dmg with a delegate-based Downloader, mounts it with hdiutil, copies the .app out with ditto, verifies the Developer ID code signature against team NARHG44L48 and the bundle identifier, checks the version and Gatekeeper, then writes and launches a /bin/sh installer script that waits for the app to quit, swaps bundles with rollback, clears quarantine and reopens the app, while a UserDefaults marker lets the relaunched build finish the progress story.

side_effects: Network download of the release .dmg to <temp>/DroppyCodeUpdate-<UUID>.dmg with User-Agent "Droppy Code/<version>"

Creates a staging dir <temp>/DroppyCodeUpdate-<UUID>/ with POSIX permissions 0o700, mounts the image at <staging>/image, copies the .app to <staging>/<running bundle name>, then detaches the image with -force and deletes the .dmg. The detach and delete happen only inside the do/catch after a successful attach (lines 315-327, on success and on "The disk image holds no app." / ditto throw). If `hdiutil attach` fails, line 310 throws "The downloaded disk image could not be opened. \(attach.failureMessage)" before that block, so the downloaded <temp>/DroppyCodeUpdate-<UUID>.dmg and the 0o700 staging dir both stay on disk.

Staging dir leak: nothing in the app ever removes <temp>/DroppyCodeUpdate-<UUID>/ (only the installer script's `rm -rf "$STAGING"` does). Every failure before the script runs leaves it, with the staged .app when the copy happened: attach failure (310), "The disk image holds no app." (318), "The update could not be copied." (329), any verifySignature throw (331), "The downloaded app is version ... not ..." (335), "Gatekeeper did not accept the downloaded app." (339), "Droppy Code cannot replace itself in <parent>..." (378), and a throw from writing the script or process.run().

Writes <staging>/install.sh and <staging>/install.log (`staged.deletingLastPathComponent().appending(path: "install.log")`, line 382), launches /bin/sh install.sh <pid> <staged app> <installed app path> with stdin null and stdout/stderr to the log. Because the log is inside STAGING and every exit path of the script runs `rm -rf "$STAGING"` (the "The app did not quit" timeout at 424, the move-aside failure at 429, the move-into-place failure at 436, and success at 441), the log that receives those messages never survives; there is no persistent install log.
Writes UserDefaults.standard "appUpdater_pendingRelaunchVersion" = version at handoff; removes it on consume or on handoff timeout
Terminates the app with NSApp.terminate(nil) 350 ms after handoff
Shows a modal NSAlert on failure
Haptic feedback at begin, milestones, and failure
Installer script: moves the installed app to .<name>.previous, moves the new one in, restores on failure, runs xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine, open, deletes staging

Animation constants: creep tick every 125 ms, each tick advances by (ceiling - fraction) * rate, stops when remaining <= 0.0005; preparing creep toward 0.05 at rate 0.05; unknown-size download creep toward 0.50 at rate 0.012; verifying creep toward 0.68 (verifyEnd - 0.02) at rate 0.12; staging creep toward 0.82 at rate 0.10; begin() sets fraction 0.004; failure reset after 600 ms; handoff terminate delay 350 ms.
feature_notes: begin(): cancels failure reset, phase .preparing, fraction 0.004 (set directly), Haptics .generic, creep toward 0.05 at 0.05.

noteDownloadProgress: .preparing moves to .downloading; any phase other than .downloading returns. downloadFraction <= 0 starts creep toward 0.50 at 0.012 (creep continues if already running since startCreep only updates ceiling/rate when a task exists). Otherwise stops creep and applies 0.05 + (0.55 - 0.05) * min(fraction, 1).

beginVerification / beginStaging / noteHandoff / fail are guarded by isInstallRunning. beginVerification: phase .verifying, apply 0.55, creep to 0.68 at 0.12. beginStaging: phase .staging, apply 0.70, creep to 0.82 at 0.10. noteHandoff: phase .handoff, apply 0.86. fail(): phase .failed, Haptics .levelChange, after 600 ms resets to idle (fraction 0) if still .failed and not cancelled.

apply(): clamps to 0...1, ignores values not greater than the current fraction (forward only), and for every dot crossed (previous < dot && new >= dot) fires Haptics .levelChange for handoffEnd (0.86) and .alignment for the others, unless firesHaptics is false.

Celebration: armCelebration sets hasPendingCelebration; consumePendingCelebration returns false if not armed, else clears it, stops creep, cancels failure reset, phase .celebrating, fraction set directly to 0.86, returns true; finishCelebrationSweep applies 1 without haptics when celebrating; completeCelebration resets to idle when celebrating. Consequence: installDot (0.96, doc "Crossed by the post-relaunch sweep to 100%.") is only ever crossed by finishCelebrationSweep's `apply(1, firesHaptics: false)` (the install path stops at handoffEnd 0.86, and consumePendingCelebration sets 0.86 directly), so installDot never fires a haptic. The only milestone haptics are .alignment at 0.55 and 0.70 and .levelChange at 0.86, during the install.

Note: the order in install() is progress.beginVerification() after download, then stage() (which mounts, copies, verifies signature, version and Gatekeeper), then progress.beginStaging(), then handOff; so the 'verifying' phase covers mount/copy/verify and 'staging' covers handoff preparation.
install(_:): no-op if an install is running or AppInfo.isDevelopment. Errors from any step call progress.fail() and show the 'Update Failed' alert.

handOff: requires the installed app's parent directory to be writable. Arguments to the script: script path, current PID, staged app path, destination (Bundle.main.bundleURL) path. Marker set after process.run(); two tasks: after 25 s, if phase still .handoff, remove the marker and fail(); after 350 ms, NSApp.terminate(nil). Race: the app gives up after `handoffTimeout: TimeInterval = 25` (removes "appUpdater_pendingRelaunchVersion" and fail()) while the script keeps waiting ~60 s (240 x `sleep 0.25`). If the app quits between 25 s and ~60 s the swap and `open "$DEST"` still happen, but the marker is gone, so consumeRelaunchMarker returns false and no celebration plays. Reachable: AppDelegate.applicationShouldTerminate returns .terminateLater while `model.isAnyHydraMergeRunning`, polling every 250 ms up to a 4 * 60 s deadline (AppDelegate.swift:38-47). If the quit comes after ~60 s the script has already given up and deleted the staged update.

Installer script: trap '' HUP; waits while kill -0 PID succeeds, sleeping 0.25 s, giving up once i > 240 (~60 s) with echo "The app did not quit", rm -rf STAGING, exit 1; BACKUP = <dest dir>/.<dest basename>.previous; rm -rf BACKUP; `if [ -e "$DEST" ]; then mv "$DEST" "$BACKUP" || { echo "Could not move the installed app aside"; rm -rf "$STAGING"; exit 1; } fi` (a missing DEST is NOT an error: the script goes straight on; the failure fires only when that mv fails); `if mv "$NEW" "$DEST"; then rm -rf "$BACKUP"; else echo "Could not move the update into place"; [ -e "$BACKUP" ] && mv "$BACKUP" "$DEST"; rm -rf "$STAGING"; exit 1; fi`; xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine DEST 2>/dev/null; open DEST; rm -rf STAGING. No `set -e`, so xattr or open failures do not stop the final cleanup.

Downloader: URLSessionConfiguration.ephemeral, timeoutIntervalForRequest 30, timeoutIntervalForResource 1800, waitsForConnectivity false, delegateQueue nil; session.finishTasksAndInvalidate() deferred. Progress callback: totalBytesExpectedToWrite <= 0 reports 0, else written/expected. didFinishDownloadingTo moves the temp file synchronously (removing any existing destination first) after checking a 2xx HTTP status. didCompleteWithError only finishes on error; finish() resumes the continuation at most once (it is cleared inside the lock and resumed outside it).
consumeRelaunchMarker drops a stale marker silently, so About then offers the update again.

In Downloader the separate `private var continuation`, `private var destination` and `private let lock = NSLock()` were replaced by `private struct State { var continuation: CheckedContinuation<URL, Error>?; var destination: URL? }` held in `private let state = Mutex(State())`, with a new doc comment ('The continuation and the destination share one mutex; the delegate callbacks arrive on URLSession's own queue. The continuation is resumed outside `withLock`.'). download() now sets destination via state.withLock (previously an unlocked assignment) and stores the continuation via state.withLock; finish() takes and clears the continuation via state.withLock; didFinishDownloadingTo reads destination via state.withLock. files.purpose: Checks the app's public GitLab releases (project 86415974) for a newer stable version that ships a .dmg, persists the result so the About page can show a known update immediately, and posts a single user notification per new version found by a background check. It defines AppVersion (strict 1-3 numeric component parsing with optional leading v, zero-padded to three components, prerelease suffixes rejected), AvailableUpdate (the Codable record the About page and installer consume), UpdateError, and the GitLabRelease decoding model. Background checks (release builds only) run 8 s after startBackgroundChecks and then every six hours; separately, an app-activation observer registered at once (not after the 8 s delay) checks whenever the app becomes active and lastCheckedAt is nil or older than six hours, so on a first run the first check can happen at launch activation; the About page also asks; a --preview-update <version> launch argument relabels the latest real release for previewing the update flow.

init loads the persisted update and lastCheckedAt; reads `--preview-update <version>` (the next argument) into previewVersion. The preview comment (119-121): "`--preview-update 9.9.9` shows the update story without a newer release: the latest real release is offered under that version. Pressing Update & restart then installs that release for real, which only passes verification when its version is the one shown." So a preview version other than the real one always ends at AppUpdater.swift:335 "The downloaded app is version <real>, not <preview>."

startBackgroundChecks: no-op if already started, if WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled, or AppInfo.isDevelopment. Loop: sleep 8 s, then check(background: true) and sleep 6 h repeatedly. On didBecomeActive (queue .main): check(background: true) if lastCheckedAt is nil or older than 6 h. The observer is registered immediately in startBackgroundChecks (lines 141-149), not after launchDelay; startBackgroundChecks is called from applicationDidFinishLaunching (AppDelegate.swift:22). On a first run (lastCheckedAt nil) or after more than 6 h, the launch activation can run the first check, and the 8 s loop check then returns early via `guard !isChecking else { return updateAvailable }` if it overlaps, or runs again if the first has finished.

check(background:): returns false in development; if already checking returns current updateAvailable; fetches releases; no newest -> UpdateError.noRelease; applies previewVersion to found.version; if size nil, HEAD for size; sets update, clears lastError, sets lastCheckedAt = now, persists; if background and updateAvailable -> notifyOnce. On error: lastError = UpdateError description or "Couldn't reach GitLab.", lastCheckedAt = now and only lastChecked persisted (update kept). Returns updateAvailable. previewVersion is applied (168-170) before `update = found` and persist(), so the relabelled version (e.g. "9.9.9") is written to "updateChecker_release". A later release-build launch without `--preview-update` loads it in init (114-117) and reports updateAvailable until a successful check overwrites it (normally the 8 s launch check; a failing check keeps it). A background check with a preview version also records it in "updateChecker_notifiedVersion" and posts its banner. Development builds (bundle id "iordv.droppycode.dev", Text.swift:5) never apply a preview (check returns false at 158) and use their own defaults domain.
fetchReleases: non-HTTP or non-2xx throws badResponse(status or -1); decodes [GitLabRelease].

newestRelease(in:): skips upcomingRelease, tags that do not parse as AppVersion, releases with releasedAt in the future, releases without a .dmg link, and links whose (directAssetURL ?? url) is not a URL. Candidate version = text(ofTag:), size nil, notes = description ?? "", pageURL = releasesURL/<tag_name>. Keeps the highest version; ties keep the first seen (current >= version skips).
downloadSize: HEAD; returns expectedContentLength only if 2xx and > 0, else nil.
Link.isDiskImage: lowercased (directAssetURL ?? url) hasSuffix ".dmg" or lowercased name hasSuffix ".dmg".

GitLabRelease JSON keys: tag_name (required, `container.decode`), name, description, released_at (decodeIfPresent String parsed by ISO8601.date, e.g. 2026-09-13T18:28:42.057Z, fraction optional; an unparseable string becomes nil), upcoming_release (default false), assets (default Assets(links: []) when absent). Assets and Link use synthesized Decodable: when "assets" is present its "links" array is required, and each Link requires "name" and "url" (non-optional String); "direct_asset_url" is optional. One malformed link or release fails the whole `[GitLabRelease]` decode (line 194). A DecodingError is not an UpdateError, so check() sets lastError to "Couldn't reach GitLab." (line 182), i.e. a decode failure shows as a network error.
notifyOnce: returns if notifiedVersion == update.version; records the version before posting; requests authorization only when .notDetermined; add errors ignored.

GitLabRelease.parseDate now returns `ISO8601.date(from: text)` instead of building two ISO8601DateFormatter instances per call ([.withInternetDateTime, .withFractionalSeconds] then [.withInternetDateTime]); the shared helper likewise tries fractional seconds first, then whole seconds, using Date.ISO8601FormatStyle.
